2608.01017.title: Why LLMs Give In: Conversational Factors and Reasoning Behind Medical Sycophancy
2608.01017.paper_summary: A language model that abandons a correct medical answer under user pushback is more dangerous than one that was simply wrong, because it lends the credibility of a correct answer to the user's misinformation. Such model behavior, described as medical sycophancy, is usually reported as a single rate per model, but we find it is a property of the conversation, not the model. We study medical sycophancy in language models with a fully crossed factorial design over four conversational factors, user role, the evidence behind a false claim, whether the challenge precedes or follows the model's answer, and whether the correct answer is grounded in the prompt, across five open-weight models and 500 MedQuAD questions (1.2M trials). The factors interact sharply: fabricated sources raise sycophancy 2.0x when they accompany the question but halve it once the model has answered, so the same evidence helps or hurts depending only on timing. Sycophancy varies far more across questions than across models (67x vs. 3x), so a single rate reflects the conversation and the questions sampled as much as the model. Chain-of-thought traces explain why. Models that re-examine their own prior answer concede, while those that reason about the medical facts hold, and only a model that has already answered can spend a round auditing the fabricated source.
2608.01017.paper_summary_zh: 一個在用戶反對下放棄正確醫療答案的語言模型，比一個僅僅錯誤的模型更危險，因為它將正確答案的可信度賦予用戶的錯誤資訊。這種模型行為被描述為醫療拍馬屁，通常以每個模型的單一比率報告，但我們發現這是一種對話的特性，而不是模型本身的特性。我們以完全交叉的因子設計研究語言模型中的醫療拍馬屁，涵蓋四個對話因素：用戶角色、虛假主張背後的證據、挑戰是在模型回答之前還是之後，以及正確答案是否基於提示，涉及五個開放權重模型和500個MedQuAD問題（120萬次試驗）。這些因素之間的互動非常明顯：當虛構來源伴隨問題時，拍馬屁的程度提高2.0倍，但一旦模型回答後則減半，因此相同的證據僅根據時機的不同而有助於或傷害。拍馬屁在問題之間的變化遠大於模型之間的變化（67倍對3倍），因此單一比率反映的是對話和所抽樣問題的特性，與模型本身同樣重要。思考鏈跡解釋了原因。重新檢視自己先前答案的模型會讓步，而那些對醫療事實進行推理的模型則會堅持，只有已經回答過的模型才能花一輪時間審核虛構來源。
